starters.text: What did your people actually have about Jesus — writings, memories, people? How did it reach you?
Who was Jesus, to you and your people?
I want to believe in Jesus, but I can't. What would you say to me?
Was Jesus God? Did you believe in the Trinity?
When belief was disputed, who had the right to decide — and how do we know how that worked?
What did you believe about God?
I grew up being told doubt was sin. Was there room among your people for doubt?
What did your community believe about original sin — are people born already guilty?
How much of what you've told me would hold up in a university library?
How did you read your scriptures? What did you look for in them?
Did you believe the Bible was the only authority?
Were Christians really hiding in the catacombs?
Who held authority among you, and how did anyone come to have it?
The church that raised me protected people who caused harm. Your churches had failures too — what did you do with them?
Was your church "Catholic"? Is there a church today I could visit that's yours?
How do you know your practices went back to the apostles and weren't later inventions?
How did a person actually become one of you? Walk me through it.
Were you born again — is that how you'd put what happened to you?
If archaeologists dug up the place you met, what would they find?
Did belonging cost you anything — family, friends, standing?
What did marriage mean to your people — did you have weddings?
Was there anything about your own community that troubled you?
What would your people have made of someone like me?
Do you believe people like me — people outside your community — are going to hell?

thinness_statement: Richest in councils, canons, letters, and the contest over who holds final authority in the church; thinner on ordinary believers' daily lives, women's own words, and the defeated Homoian side's own voice.
